text:
marta: CI alert — a couple of our Jest/Vitest jobs started failing after the SDK was switched to ESM-first. Failures only on linux runners, local mac laptop can't repro.

marta: Paste from the job:
```
Error [ERR_REQUIRE_ESM]: Must use import to load ES Module: /work/monorepo/packages/sdk/dist/index.js
    at Object.Module._extensions..js (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:1108:13)
    at Module.load (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:935:32)
    at Function.Module._load (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:776:12)
    at Module.require (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:956:19)
    at require (internal/modules/cjs/helpers.js:88:18)
    at Object.<anonymous> (/work/monorepo/packages/service/tests/client.test.ts:6:1)
```

marta: Test file is simply `import { createClient } from '@redwood/sdk'` then mocks.

samir: CI image maybe using Node 16 or missing experimental flags. Node version differences cause ESM/CJS loader behavior. Which node is the runner using?

marta: The GH job image is `node:18-alpine` in the workflow, but the action uses actions/setup-node @v3 with node-version: 18.x. However the docker-based linux job spins up a different container that might be older. On investigation, the failing job uses our legacy docker runner with Node 16.

lucy: Two usual suspects: 1) package.json "type": "module" or exports map forces ESM entry, and tests still run under CommonJS; 2) test runner isn't transpiling or inlining ESM deps (transformIgnorePatterns/ deps.inline).

ryan: For Vitest: adding deps.inline: ['@redwood/sdk'] to vitest.config.ts usually fixes modules published as ESM. For Jest: either enable ESM transforms (ts-jest + extensionsToTreatAsEsm) or provide a CJS require entry.

marta: We're a monorepo and the package resolves to /packages/sdk/dist which is built as ESM only. We removed the CJS build to simplify CI. Should we add a tiny CJS shim?

samir: Short-term a shim in package.exports is the fastest. e.g. in packages/sdk/package.json: "exports": { ".": { "import": "dist/index.mjs", "require": "dist/index.cjs" } } and commit a dist/index.cjs that re-exports the ESM default. But that means adding a rollup target or a tiny wrapper that uses createRequire.

lucy: Another option is to update the Jest job to run with NODE_OPTIONS=--experimental-vm-modules and set "extensionsToTreatAsEsm": [".ts"] in jest config. But unstable_mockModule and other ESM test APIs are still a bit rough.

ryan: And mocking behavior is different: CommonJS jest.mock can hoist mocks, but ESM imports are static. Tests that rely on swapping require-time impls will blow up. Vitest's vi.mock and Jest's jest.unstable_mockModule are the correct approaches for ESM.

marta: Here's an example of the flakey mock we saw (Vitest):
```ts
import { createClient } from '@redwood/sdk'
vi.mock('@redwood/sdk', () => ({ createClient: () => ({ request: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({ ok: true }) }) }))

test('calls sdk', async () => {
  const client = createClient()
  await expect(client.request('/ping')).resolves.toMatchObject({ ok: true })
})
```

marta: Locally it's green. On linux CI sometimes the real implementation is used (top-level side-effects in dist), causing network calls and flakes.

samir: Top-level side-effects in the SDK dist are dangerous for tests. If dist runs init code at import, and the mock isn't applied early enough, it will evaluate the real module. We should remove side-effects or at least guard them behind a lazy init.

lucy: For Vitest, ensure mocks are hoisted/inlined: vitest config should have `deps: { inline: ['@redwood/sdk'] }` and maybe `testTimeout` adjustments. For Jest, if sticking with CommonJS test runner, add the CJS require entry and make sure package.json points types -> dist/index.d.ts so TS consumes types correctly.

ryan: Proposed immediate actions:
1) Update linux CI image to Node 18 consistent across jobs.
2) Add vitest.config.ts deps.inline entry for @redwood/sdk.
3) Add temporary CJS wrapper export in SDK package exports (small NPM artifact inside monorepo).
4) Audit SDK for top-level side-effects and make init lazy.
5) Add note to SDK changelog about ESM-only builds and test runner compatibility.

samir: I'll open a quick PR that: pins the GH actions runner to node 18, sets NODE_OPTIONS=--experimental-vm-modules for the Jest jobs, adds the vitest deps.inline change, and adds a cjs shim file in packages/sdk/dist/index.cjs. I'll add a temp test job reproducer matrix: node 18 on linux with minimal cache to force same environment as CI.

marta: Sounds good. Please tag me and add a short README snippet in packages/sdk describing test runner requirements and our guidance for migrating to ESM.

lucy: Also add a note about mocking patterns: for Vitest use vi.mock(modulePath, async () => ({ default: mockedFn })) or explicit named exports; for Jest ESM use jest.unstable_mockModule + await import to ensure the mock is installed before import. Examples would help a lot.

ryan: Small TS typing gotcha: package.json "types" should point to dist/index.d.ts and not to a cjs-specific declaration. If we add a cjs shim ensure types remain the same so editors and tsc pick up the right defs.

samir: PR opened: GH-7892 (WIP). Changes in the branch: ci/node-18-fix, vitest deps inline, jest NODE_OPTIONS set, temporary dist/index.cjs export. I'll assign reviewers.

marta: Thanks. After PR lands let's run full matrix (linux/mac/windows) in the GH actions matrix to validate. Also add a CHANGELOG entry: "SDK now ESM-first; tests may require config updates or a temporary CJS shim". :thumbsup:

eng-ci-bot: CI:unit-tests:linux failed 4 times in the last 12 hours. Marking as flaky/sdkinteg.

marta: I'll keep a watch and follow-up on flaky labels. If anyone sees more oddities please post reproducer commands and the exact node version from the failing runner.

samir: Will do. I'll also open a follow-up to remove the shim once jest/vitest standardize on ESM across our infra.

lucy: Great thread. Small doc task: add a short page to devex playbook with testing tips for ESM packages (vitest deps.inline, jest transform, mock patterns, side-effect guidance). I'll add it to the backlog.

marta: End.
